html:
Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and journalist, best known for One Hundred Years of Solitude. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.

He grew up with his grandparents in Aracataca, a small town in the banana country of northern Colombia. His grandmother's way of telling strange events in a flat, matter of fact voice became the voice of his fiction. He worked for years as a reporter before his novels made him famous.

His books mix the everyday with the impossible: a girl rises to heaven while hanging out the washing, a rain lasts nearly five years. This style, called magic realism, became the trademark of the Latin American Boom of the 1960s and 1970s.

  • One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967)
  • The Autumn of the Patriarch (1975)
  • Chronicle of a Death Foretold (1981)
  • Love in the Time of Cholera (1985)

He lived much of his life in Mexico City, and was a friend of Fidel Castro. Colombians called him Gabo.
sum: Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and journalist, best known for One Hundred Years of Solitude. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.
